name: Milk Pudding Sauce
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ teaspoonful arrow-root or corn-starch, wet with cold milk
ingredients.originalText: ½ teaspoonful arrow-root or corn-starch, wet with cold milk

instructions.text: Rub the butter into the sugar, add the beaten eggs, and work all to a creamy froth.
Wet the corn-starch and put in next with the spice—finally, pour in by the spoonful the boiling milk, beating well all the time.
Set within a saucepan of boiling water five minutes, stirring all the while, but do not let the sauce boil.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub the butter into the sugar, add the beaten eggs, and work all to a creamy froth.
2. Wet the corn-starch and put in next with the spice—finally, pour in by the spoonful the boiling milk, beating well all the time.
3. Set within a saucepan of boiling water five minutes, stirring all the while, but do not let the sauce boil.
